subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Amplification: Transistors Boost Signals
description: Learn Amplification: Transistors Boost Signals in one minute.

hook.text: A microphone produces millivolts. A speaker needs volts. A transistor bridges the gap.

buildup.text: In the active region, output current tracks input changes — scaled up by gain.

discovery.text: Multi-stage amplifiers chain transistors. Each stage multiplies gain further.

twist.text: Too much gain causes distortion. Engineers use negative feedback to keep it clean.

climax.text: Op-amps, audio amps, and RF amplifiers all rely on transistor gain.

punchline.text: A weak signal in, a strong signal out — amplification in action.

quiz.question: Why do engineers use negative feedback in amplifiers?
options: To increase the gain as much as possible
To reduce distortion and stabilize the output
To convert AC signals into DC signals
